name: LM5088MHX-2_NOPB
title: LM5088, LM5088-Q1: 4.5 V to 75 V non-synchronous buck controller with emulated current mode
summary: A step-down controller for 4.5 V to 75 V inputs that drives one external high-side N-channel MOSFET from a bootstrap supply, with a Schottky diode as the freewheeling element. It uses peak current mode control with an internally rebuilt current ramp, runs at 50 kHz to 1 MHz set by one resistor, accepts a sync clock, and regulates FB to 1.205 V ±1.5 %. A built-in 7.8 V bias regulator, three-level enable, soft start and thermal shutdown complete it. LM5088-1 adds ±5 % frequency dithering; LM5088-2 (as in LM5088MHX-2/NOPB) adds a hiccup overload timer. 16-pin HTSSOP with exposed pad; LM5088-Q1 is the AEC-Q100 version.
key_figures: 50 kHz to 1 MHz, one resistor; sync input

notes: The digit after MH, MHX, QMH or QMHX picks the version: -1 has the DITH pin and spread-spectrum dithering, -2 has the RES pin and the hiccup overload timer.
A Q after LM5088 marks the automotive LM5088-Q1, qualified to AEC-Q100 grade 1 (-40 °C to +125 °C ambient), HBM ESD class 2 and CDM class C5.
MH parts ship in tubes of 92; MHX parts ship on reels of 2500.
Body size of the HTSSOP (16) is 5.00 mm × 4.00 mm nominal.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input of the controller, 4.5 V to 75 V in operation.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Three-level enable. Under 0.4 V the part is in its low-power shutdown; from 0.4 V to 1.2 V it is in standby; above 1.2 V it runs. A resistor divider from VIN can set a line undervoltage threshold. An internal 5 µA pull-up turns the controller on when the pin is left floating.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft start. An external capacitor on this pin is charged by 11 µA from inside; while SS is under the 1.2 V reference its voltage sets the error amplifier's reference. Pulled low in standby, VCC undervoltage and thermal shutdown. Driving it from a supply below 1.2 V makes that voltage the reference, for tracking.

pins.name: RAMP
pins.function: Ramp capacitor to GND sets the slope of the emulated current ramp. Recommended range 100 pF to 2000 pF.

pins.name: RT/SYNC
pins.function: A resistor to GND sets the oscillator frequency, 50 kHz to 1 MHz recommended. An external clock faster than the programmed frequency may be AC-coupled in with a small capacitor; RT must remain fitted when synchronised.

pins.name: COMP
pins.function: Error amplifier output. The loop compensation network goes between COMP and FB.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Inverting input of the error amplifier, taken from the output divider. It regulates to 1.205 V.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Output voltage sense; wire it straight to the regulated output.

pins.name: DITH
pins.function: LM5088-1 only. Capacitor to GND is ramped up and down by 27 µA sources, moving the oscillator between -5 % and +5 % of the RT frequency. Tied to GND, dithering is off.

pins.name: RES
pins.function: LM5088-2 only. Hiccup timing capacitor. In normal running a 25 µA sink holds it low; in any cycle that hits the cycle-by-cycle limit the sink stops and 50 µA charges it. At 1.2 V the HG drive stops and a 1 µA sink discharges the capacitor; switching starts again when RES falls below 0.2 V.

pins.name: CSG
pins.function: Low-side (ground) end of the current sense resistor.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Current sense input for the freewheeling diode current. An internal sample-and-hold measures the voltage on the external sense resistor at the end of the switch off-time; that sample is the DC base of the emulated current ramp.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node; connects to the source of the external N-channel MOSFET.

pins.name: HG
pins.function: High-side gate drive; connects to the gate of the external MOSFET.

pins.name: BOOT
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the gate driver. A capacitor from BOOT to SW is needed; an internal diode recharges it from VCC during each off period.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Bias regulator output, 7.8 V typical; below regulation it follows VIN. Needs a 0.1 µF to 10 µF ceramic capacitor. An external 8.3 V to 13 V supply on this pin lowers the dissipation inside the part.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed pad, not connected electrically. Solder it to the ground plane to lower thermal resistance.

circuits.title: LM5088-1 application, 5.5-55 V in, 5 V at 7 A
circuits.description: A 250 kHz step-down converter built round the dithering version. Q1 switches the input onto the SW node, driven from HG with C13 as its bootstrap capacitor; D1 carries the inductor current while Q1 is off, and that current returns through the 10 mΩ sense resistor R5, whose two ends go to CS and, as a Kelvin pair, to CSG. R6 and C20 damp ringing across the diode. Five 2.2 µF ceramics and C6 filter the input, C7 holds up VCC, and 470 µF plus two 47 µF and a 0.1 µF filter the 5 V output. R8 over R9 feed back to FB; R7 sits between the output and that divider. R1 and R2 set the enable threshold from VIN, R3 sets 250 kHz and C8 couples an outside clock into RT/SYNC, C9 is the ramp capacitor, C10 the soft-start capacitor, and R4, C12 and C11 compensate the error amplifier. D2, R10, C16 and C21 are positions left empty. C14, 0.1 µF on DITH, sets how fast the switching frequency sweeps.

parts.note: dual common-cathode Schottky, both anodes joined

circuits.title: LM5088-2 application, 5.5-55 V in, 5 V at 7 A

operation.text: Peak current mode control, but the current ramp is rebuilt inside the part rather than measured through the switch, so no leading-edge spike needs blanking and very short on-times stay controllable at high input voltage. Current mode gives line feedforward, cycle-by-cycle limiting and simple compensation. The frequency is set between 50 kHz and 1 MHz.

LM5088-1 spreads its switching frequency ±5 % for lower conducted and radiated EMI; LM5088-2 has instead a restart timer for overload. Both have the low-dropout bias regulator, three-level enable, soft start, tracking and oscillator sync. LM5088-Q1 is the AEC-Q100 grade 1 automotive part.

VIN, up to 75 V, feeds an internal low-dropout regulator that makes VCC (7.8 V) for the controller and gate driver, current limited to 30 mA. HG starts switching and soft start begins once VCC passes 4 V and EN is above 1.2 V; switching stops if VCC falls below 3.8 V or EN below 1.1 V. Below 7.8 V of input the pass device is fully on and VCC follows VIN less the drop in it. The VCC capacitor is chosen for start-up and is at least 0.1 µF. An outside supply above 8.2 V on VCC switches the regulator off and saves dissipation; the pass transistor has a diode from VCC to VIN that must stay reverse biased.
Ringing on VIN during line or load steps must not exceed the 76 V absolute maximum; good bypass capacitors close to VIN and GND and a careful board are needed.

EN below 0.4 V: low-current shutdown. 0.4 V to 1.2 V: standby, with VCC running but the switch off and SS held low. Above 1.2 V, with VCC above its threshold, SS and switching are released. Both thresholds have 100 mV hysteresis. A divider from VIN sets the start-up voltage; the internal 5 µA pull-up must be counted in it. Inside, EN goes through 1 kΩ to an 8 V zener: past 8 V the pin draws 1 mA more per volt, and it must stay below 14 V.

One resistor from RT/SYNC to GND sets the frequency and belongs right at the pin. To lock to a clock, a rising edge is capacitively coupled into RT/SYNC; it must go above 3 V and last under 150 ns. The free-running frequency is set about 15 % under the clock. A clock above twice the free-running frequency can upset the modulator.

The error amplifier compares FB with the 1.205 V reference and puts its output on COMP for the compensation parts; a type II network (integrator pole, phase-boosting zero in mid band, high-frequency noise pole) normally suffices. COMP is then set against the emulated current signal by the PWM comparator.

The rebuilt current signal has two parts. Its DC level is the diode current sampled across the sense resistor between CS and CSG just before the switch turns on again. Its rising slope comes from an internal current, set by VIN − VOUT, charging the capacitor on RAMP. For correct emulation the capacitor is matched to the inductor and sense resistor, and it connects straight to the RAMP and GND pins.

Above 50 % duty, peak current mode can break into subharmonic oscillation, seen as alternating long and short pulses on SW. The fixed 25 µA part of the ramp current adds slope compensation. Above 5 V out, especially at low input, more may be needed: a resistor from VCC to RAMP adds it. A ramp capacitor below the calculated value also raises slope compensation; one far off in either direction makes the PWM misbehave.

Dropout voltage is VIN(min) − VOUT and is fixed mainly by the maximum duty cycle, that is by frequency and the forced off-time. The off-time (365 ns max) is what the bootstrap recharge and diode-current sample need. When the controller senses dropout it lowers its frequency, continuing as VIN falls until it reaches about one third of the RT frequency; below that regulation is lost. Once the input recovers the frequency returns to the RT value. In normal operation the circuit has no effect.

A capacitor from DITH to GND turns dithering on; DITH tied to GND turns it off. The capacitor is charged and discharged between 1.14 V and 1.26 V, a triangle about 1.2 V, and this moves the oscillator from -5 % to +5 % of its RT frequency. A smaller capacitor sweeps faster; the sweep must stay much slower than fSW. On the evaluation board the conducted emission peak falls by about 10 dB with dithering on.

When the emulated current signal passes 1.2 V the cycle ends. With a shorted output the VOUT term of the ramp current drops to zero, the ramp steepens and the duty cycle shrinks at once. Separately, a comparator watches the switch's drain-source voltage while it is on and turns it off immediately if that exceeds 1.5 V, guarding against cases such as inductor saturation.

Each cycle that ends in current limit puts 50 µA into the RES capacitor over the next cycle; each cycle without it takes 27 µA out. If RES reaches 1.2 V CSS is emptied completely, RES is discharged at 1.2 µA, and at 0.2 V a normal soft start begins; a lasting overload repeats this, and once it clears the 27 µA sink holds RES at ground. Three uses: RES grounded gives cycle-by-cycle limiting only, with no hiccup; a capacitor gives a set number of limited cycles before hiccup, so short overloads ride through and long ones dissipate little; driving RES above 1.2 V from outside (say from an over-temperature or overvoltage detector) forces the restart sequence. CRES is no less than 0.022 µF; t2, the cool-down, is the 1.2 µA discharge time.

FB is regulated to the lower of SS and the 1.205 V reference, so the output ramps linearly as 11 µA charges CSS from 0 V. SS is clamped 120 mV above FB, so after a dip out of regulation the output recovers under soft-start control with less overshoot.

A high-current, level-shifted driver controls an external N-channel MOSFET from a bootstrap capacitor, a ceramic connected right across BOOT and SW, which an internal diode tops up from VCC whenever the switch is off. At high duty HG is held off each cycle for up to 365 ns so the capacitor refills. A pre-charge MOSFET from SW to GND turns on during that forced off-time, which keeps the capacitor charged at light or pre-biased loads when SW does not stay low.
At about 165 °C junction the controller goes into a low-power reset, turning off the gate driver and the bias supply.

Targets: 5 V out, 5.5 V to 36 V in, 7 A maximum load, 250 kHz. Chosen parts: RT 24.9 kΩ (24.5 kΩ calculated), L 6.8 µH (40 % ripple), RS 10 mΩ (limit 10 % over full load), CRAMP 270 pF NPO, 5 % or better (340 pF calculated), output 470 µF aluminium with 10 mΩ ESR in parallel with two 47 µF ceramics (ESR below 15 mΩ needed for 50 mV ripple; 100 mV transient), input five 2.2 µF 100 V ceramics, VCC 1 µF, bootstrap 0.1 µF (at least 0.022 µF), CSS 0.022 µF for about 2 ms, RFB1 1.62 kΩ and RFB2 5.11 kΩ, RUV2 54.9 kΩ and RUV1 16.2 kΩ for 5 V start-up, restart delay 500 µs, MOSFET SI7148DP (30 nC, 10 ns rise, 12 ns fall), diode MBRB2060 60 V Schottky (0.6 V at 7 A, 50 °C), CCOMP 0.015 µF and RCOMP 18 kΩ (zero at 0.6 kHz, crossover target 15 kHz), CHF 100 pF.

Ripple is largest at the highest input voltage. More ripple means a smaller inductor but more work for the output capacitor. The inductor must carry the peak current without saturating; in overload that peak is held to VCS(TH)/RS, and with the output shorted at maximum input the part is checked hot, since saturation current falls with temperature.

Output ripple is set mostly by ESR; load step deviation by both capacitance and ESR. While the switch conducts, the input capacitors deliver the bulk of its current; size them for RMS current, about IOUT/2, and use low-ESR ceramics. Line inductance and ceramic input capacitors can ring on connection and push VIN past its rating: add an aluminium capacitor with some ESR or make CIN more than ten times LIN, minding the aluminium part's ripple rating. Tantalum capacitors are not used at the input. The VCC capacitor is a low-ESR ceramic of at least 0.1 µF; the bootstrap capacitor a low-ESR ceramic of at least 0.022 µF next to the pins, since its peak current can reach several amperes.

The lower divider resistor is picked so that 1.2 V across it passes between 100 µA and 1 mA. For the EN divider RUV2 is 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ, with a capacitor across RUV1 for filtering. With EN floating the controller starts once VCC reaches 4.0 V.

The MOSFET's VDS rating must exceed the highest input plus ringing, and low gate charge cuts switching time and drive loss; gate charging loss is spent inside the controller. A Schottky freewheeling diode is required in every application, for its clean reverse recovery and low forward drop. Its reverse rating covers maximum input plus margin for SW ringing; the worst case for its dissipation is a shorted output. From 5 A load upward at high input a D2PAK diode is advised.

An RC across the power diode cuts ringing and spikes on SW, which can otherwise exceed the ratings of the controller or diode. The values are found by experiment with very short leads; 3 Ω to 10 Ω suits the currents involved. More capacitance damps more but loses more; the resistor's dissipation does not depend on its value.

RCOMP and CCOMP make a type II network; the amplifier's DC gain is 80 dB. Its zero is put on the modulator pole, so the loop has a single-pole response through crossover and 90° phase margin. The zero sits at least ten times below crossover; raising RCOMP while lowering CCOMP in step lowers the gain, which above the zero is RCOMP/RFB2, about 3.56 (11 dB) in the example. Loop gain in dB is modulator gain plus amplifier gain. Without a network analyser the design can be checked by load steps, aiming for little overshoot and a damped response. CHF reduces noise pickup on the amplifier but adds a pole and so is kept small.

Most loss is in MOSFET conduction and switching, diode conduction, inductor DCR and the controller's VIN and VCC currents; the rest is about 2 %. At 7 A out and 55 V in the controller dissipates about 850 mW; on the evaluation board its junction-to-ambient resistance is about 40 °C/W in still air, giving 25 + 40 × 0.9 = 61 °C at 25 °C ambient. Vias under the exposed pad lower the junction temperature a lot; copper area, via count and airflow matter most, and voids in the pad's solder joint badly reduce heat flow.

Two loops carry fast-switched current: input capacitors, MOSFET, inductor, load; and output capacitor ground, PGND, sense resistor, Schottky, inductor, load. Keep both small. Use a ground plane to join the input and output capacitor grounds and PGND. Run the quiet grounds (CSS, RT, CRAMP) straight to the GND pin. Tie GND and PGND together through a top copper area under the whole part, with several vias down to the ground plane. Put the input capacitor ground as near the current sense ground as possible. CS and CSG run as a Kelvin pair to the sense resistor.
